anomaly_def.Name: Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly + Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Concurrent sessions serialize on hot buffer pages or latches, causing page-level stalls despite adequate overall memory size.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : Underlying disks or storage fabric reach their throughput/IOPS ceiling, stretching read- and write-service times well beyond the engine’s expectations.
Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly : Kernel-enforced quotas on file descriptors, shared memory, async-I/O contexts, or threads are exhausted, blocking further resource acquisition by the database process.

When all three conditions arise together, the wait profile is dominated by a chaotic mix of buffer-busy/latch waits, abnormally long I/O latencies, and intermittent "cannot allocate <kernel object>" errors. Checkpoint, buffer flush, and log-flush events stay in flight far longer than usual, keeping dirty pages pinned and intensifying latch contention. CPU usage oscillates between spin-waiting on latches and idle periods while sessions sleep on I/O or kernel resource waits. Connection spikes, bulk loads, or index maintenance can suddenly tip the system into a state where new back-end or parallel workers fail to start, even as existing sessions hang on buffer pins.

Causal chain: Saturated storage slows every page read and dirty-page write, lengthening the window during which pages remain pinned and latches are held. Extended latch hold times magnify buffer-cache contention, increasing the number of concurrent sessions stalled in spin loops or waiting queues. To compensate, the engine issues more outstanding I/O and spawns additional background workers, pushing file handles, async-I/O rings, and thread counts toward their OS limits. Once those limits are hit, further I/O submission or worker creation is denied by the kernel, creating a feedback loop where buffers cannot be flushed or read, latches remain locked, and the transaction and query workload deteriorates rapidly.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds to wait for a block to be written to a connection before aborting the write.
entry.trigger_condition: The server waits longer than net_write_timeout while writing a block to the client connection.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
